title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: these are 1965-69 notes on crystals and de Rham cohomology. The loose handwritten sheet sits among typed and annotated EGA IV §18.13 drafts. The first line ends a previous example: some ring satisfying conditions (a) gets a canonical divided-power (PD) structure on pA, presumably a Z_(p)-algebra without p-torsion, as for W(k) or Z_p.

Example 3 asks when a principal ideal πA carries divided powers.
- Setting: A is an integral domain whose residue characteristics are only p and 0, and π is an element with A/πA of residue characteristic p.
- Question: when can one form π^(n) = π^n/n!?
- Specialisation: A is a discrete valuation ring, so A is torsion-free and the PD structure, if it exists, is unique: γ_n(x) = x^n/n!.

The argument:
1. The condition is π^n/n! ∈ A for all n, i.e. n·v(π) − v(n!) ≥ 0 for all n.
2. Let e = v(p) be the absolute ramification index. Then v(N) = e·v_p(N) for every integer N.
3. The condition becomes v(π) ≥ e·v_p(n!)/n for all n, i.e. v(π) ≥ e·λ(p), where λ(p) = sup_n v_p(n!)/n.
4. Legendre's formula v_p(n!) = (n − s_p(n))/(p−1) gives λ(p) = 1/(p−1).
5. Hence the criterion v(π) ≥ e/(p−1). For π a uniformiser (v(π) = 1) this becomes e ≤ p−1.

Purpose: to decide which ideals in mixed-characteristic bases can serve as PD ideals (p ∈ ideal) for crystalline cohomology.
errors: Minor: the supremum λ(p) = 1/(p−1) is never attained, since v_p(n!)/n < 1/(p−1) for every n. The final criterion is still exactly right, because n = p^k makes the ratio approach the bound.

Not an error but an omission: the note does not distinguish the existence of divided powers (e ≤ p−1) from topological or PD-nilpotence (e < p−1). The latter is what is actually needed in many crystalline arguments and in Fontaine's work.

ideas.what: Canonical divided powers on pA for p-torsion-free A, e.g. pZ_p or pW(k)
ideas.modern_name: PD structure on (p) in W(k) / Z_(p)-algebras
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968); Berthelot, Cohomologie cristalline (LNM 407)

ideas.what: Criterion: the maximal ideal of a DVR with absolute ramification index e has divided powers iff e ≤ p−1; more generally πA has divided powers iff v(π) ≥ e/(p−1), via Legendre's formula
ideas.modern_name: PD condition e ≤ p−1 for ramified bases
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; standard in Berthelot (1974), Berthelot–Ogus, Fontaine, Raynaud
ideas.where_published: Standard in Berthelot, Cohomologie cristalline; Berthelot–Ogus, Notes on crystalline cohomology

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct, routine computation of the well-known e ≤ p−1 criterion for divided powers on a ramified DVR. It is historically mildly interesting as an early Grothendieck working note on this point, but nothing here is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'corps résiduels soient p et 0' should read as residue characteristics p and 0, i.e. 'caractéristiques résiduelles'.
The marginal note reads roughly 'déterminer λ(p)' and refers to computing the supremum. 'Legendre' is written above λ(p) = Sup_n v_p(n!)/n = 1/(p−1).
The line 'qui est ≤ 1' refers to λ(p) ≤ 1.
